A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARSO and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete 25-page versions support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v5 reports original CARSO experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet-200, including robustness results and aggregation analyses.

after.justification: v6 retains those experiments and adds original majority-voting, adversarial-training ablation, and alternative-classifier results.

M1.justification: The proposed representation-conditional VAE purification, balanced training batches, and doubly-exponential logit aggregation remain unchanged. Newly tested ablations and alternative classifiers do not replace the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet-200 for the main evaluations, plus MNIST and Fashion-MNIST for preliminary batch-composition investigations. The added experiments vary model configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v6 adds majority voting to the aggregation comparisons and substantially expands evaluated comparators in Tables 18–19. These include Rebuffi/Gowal classifier comparisons, MeanSparse, both Bai methods, and additional purification defenses; v5 primarily reports selected best-defense comparisons and logit/probability averaging.

E3.justification: New experiments vary clean versus adversarial training of the initial and final classifiers and test additional pretrained classifiers. Table 19 also specifies selecting the lowest reported robustness across several evaluation sources. Existing attack budgets, perturbation bounds, eight reconstructed samples, and EoT settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v6 adds majority-voting gradient-obfuscation diagnostics, ablations testing which classifier stages require adversarial training, and tests using weaker pretrained classifiers. These substantially extend the existing batch-composition, aggregation, and large-perturbation analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained stochastic reconstruction and EoT sample counts are not newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2's headline results remain unchanged, but Tables 5 and 17–19 add substantial results. For example, the new clean/AT variant achieves 0.7975 CIFAR-10 robust accuracy, and majority-vote results are explicitly flagged as unreliable. Table 19 reports Wang's CIFAR-100 robustness as 0.4266, whereas Table 2 in both versions gives 0.4267.

T1.justification: v5 Appendices A–B formally present adversarial-risk minimization, PGD updates and projection, VAE objectives, and conditional sampling. These mathematical background appendices are removed in v6, leaving brief Section 3 summaries. The CARSO aggregation equations and heuristic analysis are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution and robustness claims on the three main datasets, with a clean-accuracy penalty. The revised title and explicit aggregation mention in the conclusion restate existing contributions.

C2.justification: v6 explains why majority-vote robustness estimates are unreliable and discusses the dataset-dependent benefit of adversarially training the representation extractor. It also interprets the alternative-classifier results as supporting broader applicability. The existing Section 5.3 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v6 identifies the RobustBench snapshot used for its expanded comparison with a Git SHA and documents comparison-result provenance. Existing architecture specifications, training hyperparameters, hardware, timings, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds references to MeanSparse, Bai's adaptive smoothing and MixedNUTS, and RobustBench, supporting the expanded comparison. The main related-work discussion and claimed relationship between CARSO, adversarial training, and purification remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 revises the title, adds publication information, and makes localized wording improvements. It removes the standalone PGD/VAE background appendices and reorganizes the remaining appendices, while largely retaining the main Section 1–6 narrative.

P2.justification: v6 adds Tables 5, 17, and 18 and expands the comparison display into Table 19, incorporating v5 Table 16's clean accuracies. Existing architecture tables are relocated and renumbered; Figure 1 and the overall visual format remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v5, v6 better tests the need for adversarial training and dependence on classifier choice, and explicitly diagnoses the unreliable majority-vote evaluation. These additions improve evidential support and transparency. The expanded comparison contains a small numerical inconsistency, and the main method and headline results remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
